correctness.rationale: A finite tournament has the same counting-free FO4 theory of the random tournament at unrestricted depth iff it has the three-extension property: the four-pebble Duplicator strategy and the missing-pattern four-variable sentence establish both directions. Deleting at most t vertices preserves the property iff its minimum three-anchor pattern witness multiplicity m(q)>=t+1. Character-indicator expansion for three anchors, quadratic pair sums -1, degree-three Hasse/Weil bound 2 sqrt(q), and removal of at most 12 anchor contributions imply 8N>=q-15-2sqrt(q), covering all admissible large q. Exact exhaustive minima for all remaining q=3,7,11,19,23,27,31,43,47,59 are 0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3,4,5. Independent prime-field three-anchor enumeration and separate genuine GF(27) polynomial arithmetic reproduced the table; thus q-thresholds 19,27,43,47,59 for t=0..4 are sharp for all eligible prime powers. The finite computation does not substitute for the uniform character bound.
residual_risks: Pure-edge equality counting-free FO4 and deletion budgets 0..4 only; neither rank-5 FO nor arbitrary tournaments covered; classical Hasse bound is an invoked established theorem.

value.rationale: For a natural finite-field pseudorandom tournament family, determine exact robustness of unrestricted four-variable elementary theory against zero to four arbitrary vertex deletions. The tight thresholds include the genuine extension field of order 27 and multiple distinct exceptional transitions; meaningful finite cutoffs and the general character-sum bound jointly classify an infinite family, beyond a routine restatement of known three-extension theory.
